review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

2:1.sourceText: Σὺ δὲ λάλει ἃ πρέπει τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ.
2:1.targetText: But you—speak what is suitable [according] to the sound teaching.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English according makes the suitability relation to the dative sound-teaching phrase explicit; no Greek according-to preposition is printed in this verse.

2:2.sourceText: πρεσβύτας νηφαλίους εἶναι, σεμνούς, σώφρονας, ὑγιαίνοντας τῇ πίστει, τῇ ἀγάπῃ, τῇ ὑπομονῇ·
2:2.targetText: Elders [are] to be temperate, dignified, sober, sound in faith, in the love, in the endurance.

groups.note: The actual being infinitive εἶναι is prescriptive under the preceding speak instruction. English renders that prescribed state as are to be; both auxiliary pieces belong to this actual infinitival being predicate, not to an article or a new independent Greek finite copula.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:3.sourceText: πρεσβύτιδας ὡσαύτως ἐν καταστήματι ἱεροπρεπεῖς, μὴ διαβόλους μηδὲ οἴνῳ πολλῷ δεδουλωμένας, καλοδιδασκάλους,
2:3.targetText: Aged women, in like manner, in behavior as becomes sacred persons, not false accusers, not enslaved to much wine, teachers of good things,

groups.note: The compound adjective ἱεροπρεπεῖς means befitting holiness/sacred things; LSV expands that actual reverent-conduct designation as as becomes sacred persons, without separate Greek sacred-person nouns.

2:4.sourceText: ἵνα σωφρονίζωσιν τὰς νέας φιλάνδρους εἶναι, φιλοτέκνους,
2:4.targetText: that they may make the young women sober-minded, to be lovers of [their] husbands, lovers of [their] children,

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English their identifies the husbands belonging to the instructed women; the husband-loving compound has no separately written possessive pronoun.
Bracketed English their identifies those women’s children; the child-loving compound has no separately written possessive pronoun.

2:5.sourceText: σώφρονας, ἁγνάς, οἰκουργούς, ἀγαθάς, ὑποτασσομένας τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν, ἵνα μὴ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ βλασφημῆται.
2:5.targetText: sober, pure, keepers of [their own] houses, good, subject to their own husbands, that evil may not be spoken of the word of God.

groups.note: N1904 οἰκουργούς denotes household workers, while TR has the related house-keeping form οἰκουρούς. LSV keepers of houses retains that actual domestic/household activity head with the working-versus-keeping form distinction explicit.
The passive blaspheming predicate is rendered evil may be spoken of; the English evil/speaking/of pieces express that one actual Greek predicate, not separate Greek evil or speaking words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English possessive their own identifies whose houses are kept; N1904’s household-working compound contains no separate their/own pronoun or adjective. The actual later ἰδίοις qualifies husbands, not houses.

2:6.targetText: The younger men, in like manner, exhort [them] to be sober-minded.

groups.note: The fronted actual younger-men object is resumed in English as bracketed them after exhort. Both expressions preserve the same actual men identity, not a new Greek pronoun.

2:7.sourceText: περὶ πάντα, σεαυτὸν παρεχόμενος τύπον καλῶν ἔργων, ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ ἀφθορίαν, σεμνότητα,
2:7.targetText: Concerning all things, present yourself [as] a pattern of good works—in the teaching [with] uncorruptedness, dignity,

groups.note: The present middle participle παρεχόμενος, presenting/showing, is recast as the finite English instruction present, continuing the exhortation. The actual showing predicate is retained.

N1904 ἀφθορίαν and TR ἀδιαφθορίαν are related incorruption/integrity nouns. LSV uncorruptedness retains the actual integrity head; the extra TR final ἀφθαρσίαν has no separately printed LSV counterpart here.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English as marks the role in which yourself is presented; Greek has the pattern apposition without a separate as conjunction.
Bracketed English with connects uncorruptedness/dignity to the teaching description; N1904 has direct accusative quality nouns without a with preposition.

2:8.sourceText: λόγον ὑγιῆ ἀκατάγνωστον, ἵνα ὁ ἐξ ἐναντίας ἐντραπῇ μηδὲν ἔχων λέγειν περὶ ἡμῶν φαῦλον.
2:8.targetText: sound discourse [that is] blameless, so that he who is of the contrary may be ashamed, having nothing evil to say concerning you.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness person difference: N1904 ἡμῶν is us; LSV you follows TR ὑμῶν. These distinct first/second-person recipients are not equated.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English relative/copula connects the blameless adjective to discourse; Greek has the direct adjectival modifier without a written relative pronoun or be verb.
English supplies is in he who is of the contrary; Greek has an article plus the opposite-side phrase without a being verb.
Source-witness person difference: LSV you is TR ὑμῶν, not pinned N1904 ἡμῶν (us).

2:9.sourceText: δούλους ἰδίοις δεσπόταις ὑποτάσσεσθαι ἐν πᾶσιν, εὐαρέστους εἶναι, μὴ ἀντιλέγοντας,
2:9.targetText: Servants [are] to be subject to their own masters, to be well-pleasing in all things, not contradicting,

groups.note: The actual submitting infinitive ὑποτάσσεσθαι is prescriptive in the servant instructions; LSV recasts it as are to be subject. Both English auxiliary/state pieces express that prescribed actual predicate, not a bare article or extra original be verb.

2:10.sourceText: μὴ νοσφιζομένους, ἀλλὰ πᾶσαν πίστιν ἐνδεικνυμένους ἀγαθήν, ἵνα τὴν διδασκαλίαν τὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ κοσμῶσιν ἐν πᾶσιν.
2:10.targetText: not stealing, but showing all good steadfastness, that the teaching of God our Savior they may adorn in all things.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:11.sourceText: Ἐπεφάνη γὰρ ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ σωτήριος πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις,
2:11.targetText: For the saving grace of God has appeared to all men,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

review.note: Greek saving/salutary to all men qualifies the grace; LSV places to all men after has appeared, which can shift its English attachment to appearing. The same actual saving adjective, people and quantifier remain separate heads with that attachment difference explicit.

2:12.sourceText: παιδεύουσα ἡμᾶς, ἵνα ἀρνησάμενοι τὴν ἀσέβειαν καὶ τὰς κοσμικὰς ἐπιθυμίας σωφρόνως καὶ δικαίως καὶ εὐσεβῶς ζήσωμεν ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι,
2:12.targetText: teaching us, that denying the impiety and the worldly desires, we may live soberly, and righteously, and piously in the present age,

2:13.sourceText: προσδεχόμενοι τὴν μακαρίαν ἐλπίδα καὶ ἐπιφάνειαν τῆς δόξης τοῦ μεγάλου Θεοῦ καὶ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ,
2:13.targetText: waiting for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

review.note: The displayed Jesus Christ reverses pinned N1904 Christ Jesus. Each actual title/name retains its own original identity; the shared God-and-Savior phrase is preserved without adding a second Greek article or resolving interpretive referents by invented words.

2:14.sourceText: ὃς ἔδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἵνα λυτρώσηται ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἀνομίας καὶ καθαρίσῃ ἑαυτῷ λαὸν περιούσιον, ζηλωτὴν καλῶν ἔργων.
2:14.targetText: who gave Himself for us, that He might ransom us from all lawlessness, and might purify to Himself a special people, zealous of good works.

2:15.sourceText: Ταῦτα λάλει καὶ παρακάλει καὶ ἔλεγχε μετὰ πάσης ἐπιταγῆς· μηδείς σου περιφρονείτω.
2:15.targetText: Speak these things, and exhort and convict with all authority; let no one despise you!
